chooseHelp: Choose how to start “{{title}}”. You can add another trigger later.
scheduleHelp: Choose when Paperclip should start this routine automatically.
reviewHelp: This schedule starts the routine automatically. You can pause or change it later.
connectHelp: Copy these details into the sending app, then save its webhook settings.
checkHelp: Test that events arrive and authentication works. This won’t start the routine.
onScheduleHelp: Every day, on weekdays, or once a week.
onWebhook: When another app sends a webhook
onWebhookHelp: When something happens in GitHub, another app, or a script.
timezoneHelp: The time follows this zone, including daylight saving changes.
scheduledRunHelp: Each scheduled run creates a task for the routine’s assigned agent. Any existing webhook triggers will continue to work.
publicUrlHelp: Public services need a publicly reachable HTTPS webhook URL.
signingHelp: Paste this key into your app’s signing secret field.
headerHelp: If your app uses custom headers instead, set Authorization to Bearer followed by a space and this key.
hiddenKeyHelp: The key is hidden after leaving setup. If you haven’t saved it in your app, generate a replacement.
testOnlyHelp: Events received during setup won’t start the routine or create tasks.
sendApp: Send an event from your app
githubTestHelp: Open this webhook in your repository settings. Under Recent Deliveries, choose Redeliver on an event.
appTestHelp: Look for “Send test” in your app’s webhook settings. If it doesn’t have one, do the action that should trigger the webhook—for example, complete a deployment.
keepOpen: Keep this page open to see the test result.
rejected: Event arrived, but the key was rejected
waiting: Waiting for an event from your app…
receivedHelp: Authentication passed. No routine run or task was created.
rejectedHelp: Go back to Connect your app, update the key in your sending app, and resend. No task was created.
waitingHelp: Waiting to verify delivery and authentication. The routine is not running.
troubleshootHelp: Check that the webhook is enabled in your sending app and that its URL matches. Scripts must send POST with a JSON body.
finishActiveHelp: Finish setup to enable this webhook. Future events will start the routine; this test event won’t be replayed.
finishPausedHelp: Finish setup to save this webhook. The routine is paused; enable its automatic triggers when you’re ready. This test event won’t be replayed.
pausedScheduleHelp: The routine is paused. Enable its automatic triggers when you’re ready to use this schedule.
copyFailed: Copy failed. Select and copy the text below.
agentInstructionsHelp: Give your agent everything it needs to connect this webhook: the URL, authentication key, and step-by-step instructions.
agentPromptHelp: Paste this into your agent to connect this webhook to your routine.
warning_loopback_title: Other apps can’t reach this localhost URL
warning_loopback_message: This address points back to the machine sending the request. Services such as GitHub can’t use it to reach Paperclip on your computer.
warning_private_title: This webhook URL appears to be private
warning_private_message: Only senders with access to this network can reach this address. Apps on the public internet, such as GitHub, usually can’t deliver webhooks here.
warning_tailscale_title: This Tailscale URL may not be public
warning_tailscale_message: Tailscale Serve is private to your tailnet, even with HTTPS. Apps outside your tailnet need Tailscale Funnel or another public HTTPS address. If Funnel is already enabled for this URL, you can continue.
warning_https_title: Use HTTPS for webhooks from other apps
warning_https_message: This URL uses HTTP. Many apps require HTTPS, and HTTP does not encrypt webhook credentials or payloads.
warning_invalid_message: This is not a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL. Your sending app needs a complete address it can reach.
warningHelp: You can continue for local or private-network use. For public senders, use a publicly reachable HTTPS URL.
warningLink: Learn how to set up HTTPS and public access
